html_en:
Claude gets a look at your bank account, the case for formally verified code goes mainstream, and a machine-native future for AI outputs starts to crystallize — a day of quiet but consequential shifts in how AI embeds itself into everyday life and infrastructure.

🏦 Claude Wants to See Your Bank Statement

The most talked-about product launch of the day came from Anthropic, which introduced Personal Finance in Claude — a beta feature that lets US users on Pro, Max, and Ultra plans connect their financial accounts and ask questions about their own balances and transactions in plain English.

"Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations. It helps you understand your money, and it isn't designed to give investment advice." — @claudeai

Access is read-only — Claude can't move, manage, or invest your money — but the move is symbolically significant. Financial data is among the most sensitive a user can share, and Anthropic is betting that its trust-first positioning is enough to clear that bar. With nearly 30,000 likes on the launch tweet, the appetite appears real. Whether regulators and privacy advocates feel equally warm is a conversation that's just getting started.

🔐 The End of Human-Written Secure Infrastructure

The day's most viral technical take came from @thsottiaux, whose two-tweet thread on AI and software security racked up over 3,500 likes:

"I can confidently say that humans were not very good at writing secure infrastructure. The endstate will be hypersecure infrastructure and software for all, but we're going to go through some turbulence before we reach that." — @thsottiaux
"Formal proofs of tens of millions of lines of code are not a ridiculous thing anymore and within the realm of what should be considered when designing new systems." — @thsottiaux

This lands with extra weight alongside Amjad Masad's note that Replit's custom kernel build allows them to avoid 96% of Linux zero-day vulnerabilities — a concrete example of what "turbulence on the way to hypersecurity" looks like in practice. The implication across both: the security properties of AI-generated and AI-verified code may eventually surpass anything human developers can reliably produce at scale.

🤖 The Machine-Native Output Thesis

The most intellectually rich content of the day came from the Unsupervised Learning podcast, which hosted Jogo, CEO of TypeSave and creator of JEV — an AI model optimized for structured, machine-readable outputs rather than human prose. Watch/Listen: Ep 97: Jev Creator on Decision Models, Benchmark Fatigue & Why the Labs Missed It

His core provocation is worth sitting with:

"What percentage of those calls going into the LLMs are actually meant for human consumption — things like style matter, prose and all of that — versus for computer consumption, which is going to be very, very different? Even the most string-pilled of people will give many nines of percent for the machine-native component. It's just a question of when that will happen." — Jogo, Unsupervised Learning Ep 97

His argument: the entire field has been optimizing for human-readable string outputs when the overwhelming majority of LLM calls, in a mature agentic world, will be consumed by other software. On Anthropic's upcoming IPO and broader lab valuations, he was characteristically blunt:

"My guess is that because some people might be valuing, like, building god as basically infinite, there'll be some amount of miscalibration there. And I think that the 'let them cure cancer' is going to be like Marie Antoinette's 'let them eat cake.'" — Jogo, Unsupervised Learning Ep 97

🔁 The X-to-Vercel Flywheel Takes Shape

Guillermo Rauch laid out what he sees as a nearly complete entrepreneurial loop for the AI era:

"① Get an X sub ② Build with Bot / Cursor ③ Deploy to Vercel, scales from 0 to 🌙 ④ Launch and distribute on X ⑤ Monetize with X Money / Creators. The loop is nearly complete ♾️"

The announcement behind this: Grok and Cursor can now build, deploy, and scale via a SpaceXSI × Vercel partnership. Rauch also highlighted that Vercel Schedules — essentially cron jobs that can be defined at runtime and scale infinitely — are becoming the backbone of always-on agent products like Muse and Instinct.

"'Doing stuff for you over time' is the killer app of agents." — @rauchg

That framing aligns neatly with the viral location-based reminder prompt making the rounds from @trq212 — "remind me 30 minutes after I get home if it's been more than 5 days since I did laundry" — which accumulated over 2,300 likes as a simple, legible demonstration of ambient AI utility.

🏛️ Little Tech, Big Ambitions

Garry Tan used the week's political results as a springboard to push his "Little Tech" anti-monopoly message, framing AI distribution — not AI capability — as the defining policy challenge of the moment:

"Inventing powerful AI is only half the job. People must be able to use it to make their lives better and their businesses more productive. That gets harder when a few trillion-dollar companies can block new products from reaching them. Congress can open those markets for Little Tech. Let thousands of startups compete to lower costs and grow the economy for everyone."

Meanwhile, Aaron Levie announced a Box × NVIDIA partnership to give AI agents better access to enterprise unstructured data — the contracts, design files, and financial plans that make up 90% of corporate information — with security controls baked in. The enterprise agent race is increasingly a race for context, and whoever controls retrieval may control the workflow.
html_zh:
今天的AI圈有两个核心主题交织出现：一是AI真正进入日常生活的加速（从个人财务到代码安全），二是对这个行业基本假设的深刻质疑——估值、基准测试、以及"字符串输出"是否真的是AI的终点。

🏦 Claude 进军个人财务：无广告、只读、真实用

本周最受关注的产品发布，来自Anthropic。Claude正式在美国推出个人财务功能（Personal Finance），用户可连接自己的银行账户，用自然语言查询余额和交易记录。

"连接您选择的账户，Claude 用日常语言回答您的财务问题，基于您真实的余额和交易记录。访问权限为只读，Claude 无法转移、管理或投资您的资金。"
— @claudeai

这个功能的定位相当克制——没有理财建议，没有广告，没有推荐产品。Anthropic显然在用"不作恶"的姿态，与金融科技行业长期以来的流量变现逻辑划清界限。在AI助手争相扩展权限的时代，这种"少即是多"的设计哲学值得关注。该功能正在向美国Pro、Max和Ultra用户逐步开放。

🔐 AI时代的基础设施安全：从漏洞到形式化证明

今天技术圈里传播最广的一组推文，来自@thsottiaux。他的判断直接而有力：

"我可以自信地说，人类在编写安全基础设施方面表现并不好。最终结果将是为所有人提供超安全的基础设施和软件，但在达到那个终点之前，我们将经历一些动荡。"
— @thsottiaux
"数千万行代码的形式化证明不再是天方夜谭，在设计新系统时完全应该纳入考量。"
— @thsottiaux

与此同时，Replit CEO @amasad 也公布了一个具体数字：通过自研内核构建，Replit 能够规避 96% 的 Linux 零日漏洞。在AI编程工具爆发的背景下，沙盒安全架构正在成为差异化竞争的隐形战场。

⚙️ 从"字符串"到"机器原生"：JEV 对 AI 未来的另类判断

本期最值得深读的内容，来自播客 Unsupervised Learning 对 TypeSave CEO（JEV 创始人 Jogo）的专访。Watch/Listen: Ep 97: Jev Creator on Decision Models, Benchmark Fatigue & Why the Labs Missed It

Jogo 提出了一个颠覆性的问题：当 LLM 被软件调用时，有多少输出其实是给人类看的，又有多少是给计算机消费的？

"就算是最极端的字符串派，也会承认机器原生的调用占绝大多数——只是时间问题而已。那么，从这个认知核心出发反推，它应该长什么样？"
— Jogo，TypeSave CEO

他的核心论点是：现有 LLM 返回字符串的范式是为人类设计的，但未来软件调用 AI 的场景几乎不需要字符串——计算机想要的是结构化数据。这正是 JEV 和 RLCD（强化学习约束解码）研究方向的出发点。

他对 Anthropic 即将 IPO 的估值也有一针见血的评论：

"我感觉很多人对 Anthropic 的预期，不只是产品层面的，而是基于对 AI 未来能力的误解。有些人可能把'构建上帝'定价为无穷大，所以必然存在错误定价。那句'让它去治癌症吧'，大概会成为玛丽·安托瓦内特'让他们吃蛋糕吧'那样的历史笑柄。"
— Jogo，TypeSave CEO

🔄 平台飞轮：Vercel × Grok × X，闭环正在成型

Vercel CEO @rauchg 今天描绘了一个让人一眼看懂的创业者工作流闭环：

"① 订阅 X ② 用 Grok / Cursor 构建 ③ 部署到 Vercel，从零扩展到月球 ④ 在 X 上发布分发 ⑤ 用 X Money / Creators 变现。这个循环几乎完整了 ♾️"
— @rauchg

他还特别提到，Agent 的"杀手级应用"不是一次性任务，而是随时间持续运作：

"'随着时间推移为你做事'才是 Agent 的杀手级应用。Muse 和 Instinct 在夜间整合记忆，早上提醒你，在你最后一次交互 N 天后主动联系你……"
— @rauchg

与此同时，Box CEO @levie 宣布与 NVIDIA 合作，为企业 AI Agent 提供更强的非结构化数据检索能力——90% 的企业数据都是非结构化的，而 Agent 能否找到正确上下文，决定了它能否真正"干活"。

🏛️ Little Tech 的政治时刻

YC CEO Garry Tan 对本周政治形势表示乐观，呼吁国会借助当前的两党共识打破大科技的市场垄断：

"发明强大的 AI 只是完成了一半工作。人们必须能够用它来改善生活、提升业务效率。当少数市值万亿的公司能够阻止新产品触达用户时，这就更难实现了。国会可以为 Little Tech 打开这些市场。"
— @garrytan

这句话的潜台词很清晰：AI 的红利，不应该只流向已经掌控分发渠道的公司。这或许是整个AI行业最根本的结构性张力之一——而它正在从技术讨论，蔓延进政策议程。
